question: Does creative type perform differently on Facebook vs Instagram?
window: 2026-03-18 to 2026-08-31 for still creative (196 posts classified, 193 with reach); 2026-01-07 to 2026-08-31 for video (25 videos)
basis: Organic only. Meta's reported 'from ads' portion of reach and reactions is subtracted from every post.
note_window: Meta's Content table caps near 200 rows, so the still-creative window starts Mar 18. The Videos filter returns a short list, so video covers the full period.

top_videos_by_organic_reactions.caption: CEO message on Regence Blue Cross Blue Shield
Construction underway at the future Women's Center
As an orthopedic surgeon at Santiam Orthopedics
A closer look inside our lab
Mental health is an important part of overall health
Happy Nurses Week to the incredible nurses

findings_positive: Video is the strongest format overall: 18 median organic reactions and a 2.90% engagement rate, ahead of every still format.
On Instagram, real photographs lead decisively: 15 median reactions against 3 for designed graphics, at a 3.28% engagement rate.
Instagram engagement rates run far above Facebook across every creative type (2.4-3.3% vs 1.2%).
On Facebook, provider portrait cards are the standout: 1,933 median organic reach and 22 median reactions, the highest of any still format on either platform. Small sample of 7 posts.
On Facebook, designed graphics earn the most shares of anything measured, at 3.33 per post.
caveats: Facebook provider cards rest on 7 posts and Instagram provider cards on 6; treat those two rows as directional.
Creative classification is a manual visual judgement, not a Meta field.
Crossposted video appears under both placements; the video row is all placements combined.
